title: SLO-aware request admission with per-tenant priority lanes and regional failover
creator: Asha Verma
description: We need an admission controller for incoming inference requests that enforces SLO-driven capacity decisions at two dimensions: per-tenant priority lanes and region-aware failover. The goal is to avoid cascading failures when Redis/Kafka/DB tails spike, and to provide deterministic behavior for tenants with contracted SLOs. The controller will combine token-bucket admission, a fast-path for high-priority tenants, progressive degradation for best-effort tenants, and integration with our regional routing layer to prefer healthy backends or fallback to compatible model variants. This ticket covers the proposal, design, and a production canary implementation in the serving runtime and API gateway.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Admission controller enforces per-tenant rate/tokens with 95th-percentile latency target mapping to admission thresholds
2) High-priority lane (reserved tokens) guarantees minimal queueing for P0/P1 tenants under typical load up to committed capacity
3) Best-effort lane is subject to probabilistic shedding when downstream tail latency exceeds configured quantiles and error budget is depleted
4) Regional failover triggers within 150ms for RPCs routed through the routing layer and falls back to secondary region or degraded response per policy

5) Circuit-breaker trips on sustained 5xx or 99th-percentile latency breaches and traffic is rerouted to warm fallback or model variant; trips are visible in console and triggered automatically by SLO watcher

6) Observability: dashboards with per-tenant admission rate, dropped percentage, latency quantiles, error budget burn rate, and per-region health are available in Console; alerts for >1% shed rate for customers with SLA
7) Canary rollout plan executed with no customer-facing errors and rollback path validated
tasks: Design: finalize token-bucket parameters and mapping from tenant SLOs to reserved tokens (Asha + Priya)
Runtime: implement admission filter hook in request pipeline and token accounting (Miguel + Ethan)
Routing: add region probe and failover policy in smart router (Lena)
Circuit breaker: implement adaptive burn-window and integration with admission decisions (SRE team)
Metrics: emit per-tenant admission_allowed, admission_denied, shed_reason, token_balance metrics (Telemetry)
Documentation: update runbook and Console docs with shed semantics and SLA notes
Canary: deploy to staging group of 5 customers, observe for 72h, then gradual ramp
decisions: Use hybrid admission: reserved tokens for committed tenants + shared token pool for burst tolerance
Probabilistic shedding is preferred over blunt reject for best-effort tenants to preserve degraded success cases
Circuit-breaker uses 5min adaptive window with increased sensitivity when error budget < 20%
Regional failover will prefer warm cache replicas before spinning new capacity to keep latency bounds
We will surface 'partial' responses with a standardized header (X-Redwood-Degraded: reason) for degraded cases rather than opaque errors
notes: Trade-offs: reserving tokens isolates tenants but increases unused capacity; sharing pool improves utilization but needs fairness heuristics
Edge cases: startup storms when many tenants reconnect after region outage — added jitter and token warm-up needed
Compatibility: admission plugin must be pluggable so Dedicated/Private deployments can opt for local policy enforcement
Telemetry cardinality: per-tenant metrics can blow up; we'll roll up to tenant tiers and sample top-K tenants by usage for detailed traces
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Initial design doc posted to Confluence (link below). Reviewed with SRE and Product; agreed on hybrid token model. Action: runtime prototype.

2025-02-25: Runtime admission hook prototype merged in branch: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pulls/4321. Basic token accounting + simple reject path implemented. Found race in concurrent token refill — Miguel to fix.
2025-03-01: Added probabilistic shedding logic and integrated with circuit-breaker stub. Early staging tests show 70% reduction in tail-load amplification during synthetic downstream delay scenario.
2025-03-03: Canary gating checklist prepared; SRE approved limited rollout to staging customers; telemetry dashboards configured. Next: run 72h canary and collect SLO burn graphs.
review_feedback: Priya Kapoor (SRE): request accounting must be monotonic and support clock skew in multi-region; suggested adding lease tokens for long-running requests
Ethan Wu (Infra): prefer using existing token-bucket library for refill semantics to reduce operational risk
Monica Chen (Product): add explicit communication for customers about 'degraded' header and provide guidelines for client-side retry/backoff
testing_plan: Unit tests: token accounting edge cases, concurrent refills, lease-expiry semantics
Integration: inject artificial 95th/99th latency into Redis/Kafka and verify admission response and shedding metrics
Chaos: region partition test to validate regional failover and token rebalancing
SLA Canary: run 72-hour staged canary with 5 low-volume customers, compare SLO burn vs baseline
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge feature-flagged code to main and enable for internal staging only
Step 2: Canary enable for 5 customers (low volume) for 72h; observe shed rates and latency
Step 3: Gradual ramp to 20% production traffic with automated rollback on shed-rate or error thresholds
Step 4: Full ramp if no regressions after 1 week
monitoring: Dashboards: per-tenant admission rate, shed %, tail latency, token balance histograms, error budget burn rate
Alerts: pager on >1% shed for any SLA tenant for >10min, or >5% shed for any tenant for >2min
SLO watcher integration: admission decisions get annotated and used by SLO burn estimator
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag off for runtime admission plugin (immediate revert path)
If rollback not sufficient, route traffic to previous stable router via traffic manager and revoke token reservations
post_release_notes: Documented API header X-Redwood-Degraded and semantic meanings
Guidance added to Console on interpreting shed metrics and recommended customer actions
Follow-up ticket proposed to add per-tenant SLA billing reconciliation when shedding occurs: ENG-87270
